title: Historical unresolved-family human review queue
purpose: Prepare a compact, provenance-preserving review queue for the two strongest unresolved third-family candidates without exposing machine verdicts as human instructions or changing generator/public status.

review_policy.reason: This is a philological/syntactic review rather than a public naturalness A/B test; source provenance is necessary to judge whether recombined clauses remain interpretable.

questions.prompt: Can the five ku be parsed as one coherent classical-Japanese sentence or tightly connected utterance without adding omitted material that is not independently justified?
Are the critical mirrored boundary shifts lexically and morphologically defensible in this candidate, rather than merely character-reversal artifacts?
Does the recombination preserve the source-local scene and discourse role closely enough that the moved factor does not create an unexplained semantic jump?
Record the smallest span that still prevents a confident parse. Do not repair it from palindrome expectation.

candidates.reading: なかきよのきつるみそらはむすめよめすむはらそみるつきのよきかな
known_supported_points: D=むす is retained inside the source-specific shoju-add-109 corridor
outer donor contributes a night/moon frame compatible with the host's moon/family scene

candidates.reading: やとちかくまはるなかたひきよくゆくよきひたかなるはまくかちとや
known_supported_points: all five ku are attested at the Yamauchi poem-specific scholarly-transcription layer across sources 90 and 93
やとちかく and くかちとや recur in the same travel series via poem 91
known_unresolved_spans: cross-ku whole-sentence connection between donor outer frame and host middle
source-glyph restoration for kana-rich spans remains intentionally unresolved

adjudication_rule.unsupported: demote/hold the candidate but do not generalize rejection to the source factor globally

next_action: Use this queue only when a qualified human philological review is available; until then keep both candidates at their existing research statuses.
